name: Athens
notes: Naval hegemon of the Delian League

name: Sparta
notes: Land-based hegemon of the Peloponnesian League

name: Corinth
notes: Greek polis, often aligned with Sparta

name: British India
notes: Major source of manpower for British forces in Malaya, with Indian units forming a large portion of frontline troops under British command.

name: British Malaya
notes: Colonial territory serving as the operational theatre, whose geography and infrastructure shaped both the Japanese advance and the Allied defensive failure.

name: Nazi Germany
notes: Aggressor state attempting to gain air superiority over Britain.

name: British Commonwealth
notes: Provided pilots and support personnel from countries such as Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

name: Royal Air Force
notes: Air arm of the United Kingdom responsible for air defense under Fighter Command.

name: Luftwaffe
notes: Air arm of Nazi Germany responsible for offensive air operations against Britain.

name: RAF Fighter Command
notes: Operational command responsible for air defense of Britain, led by Hugh Dowding.

name: Chinese Communist Forces
notes: Communist military forces led by Mao Zedong

name: South African Republic
notes: Also known as Transvaal, Boer republic

name: Orange Free State
notes: Independent Boer republic allied with Transvaal

name: Qing China
notes: Nominal sovereign power over Manchuria but militarily weak and politically divided

name: Korean Empire
notes: Korean state caught between Russian and Japanese strategic ambitions

name: French Third Republic
notes: French government with financial ties to the Russian Empire

name: Upper Canada
notes: British colony forming the main Canadian land theatre during the war

name: Lower Canada
notes: British colony supporting defense of Canada and control of the St. Lawrence corridor

name: Native Confederacy
notes: Indigenous alliance led primarily by Tecumseh resisting American expansion into the Northwest Territory

name: Red Stick Creek
notes: Militant faction of the Creek Confederacy allied indirectly with British interests against the United States

name: Royal Navy
notes: British naval force conducting blockade operations and amphibious attacks

name: United States Navy
notes: American naval force operating in the Atlantic and Great Lakes theatres

name: British Army
notes: British regular army forces deployed in Canada and the Chesapeake campaigns

name: United States Army
notes: American land forces conducting invasions of Canada and frontier campaigns

name: Canadian Militia
notes: Local colonial militia units supporting British defense operations in Canada

name: Shawnee
notes: Indigenous nation associated with Tecumseh and resistance to American expansion

name: Kalmar Union
notes: Personal union linking Denmark Norway and Sweden under a common monarch while preserving separate laws and institutions.

name: Hanseatic League
notes: Commercial network of North German trading cities heavily involved in Baltic commerce.

name: City of Lübeck
notes: Leading Hanseatic city with major influence over Baltic trade and Scandinavian politics.

name: Swedish Privy Council
notes: Council of Swedish nobles and bishops that competed for influence over royal authority and union policy.

name: Danish Crown
notes: Royal administration and military structure supporting centralized union rule from Copenhagen.

name: Sture Faction
notes: Swedish anti-union aristocratic network led by the Sture regents.

name: Vasa Faction
notes: Political and military coalition supporting Gustav Vasa during the final break from the Kalmar Union.

name: Bergslagen Communities
notes: Mining and iron-producing communities that formed the economic backbone of several Swedish uprisings.

name: Dalarna Peasants
notes: Armed free peasants and bergsmän from Dalarna who repeatedly mobilized in Swedish political conflicts.

name: Archbishopric of Uppsala
notes: Major ecclesiastical power center involved in Swedish political struggles.

name: Union Royal Army
notes: Military forces loyal to the Kalmar Union monarchs during repeated conflicts in Sweden.

name: Free City of Lübeck
notes: Major Hanseatic trading city allied with Denmark against Sweden

name: Kingdom of Poland-Lithuania
notes: Regional Baltic power observing and influencing Scandinavian affairs
